transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. I... well, I came in today because I just can't seem to shake this incredibly heavy, hopeless feeling. It’s like... you know, I work as a civil engineer, and I spend all day calculating loads and stresses, making sure things don't fall apart, but right now, it feels like everything I’ve built—especially after my divorce, which was a whole other nightmare of trying to reconstruct my life from the ground up—has just completely collapsed. And I’m just sitting under all the rubble. I try to get up, I try to go to work and look at the blueprints and talk to the contractors, but this weight, it's just pressing down on me so hard that I can barely breathe sometimes. It’s not just a bad day, it’s this persistent, crushing sensation that nothing is ever going to be okay again, no matter how hard I try to engineer a way out of it.
Have you experienced episodes like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Well, that's the thing... I mean, I've had times where I felt down, sure. Everyone gets sad, right? Especially with the divorce, there were days where I just wanted to stay in bed and pull the covers over my head. But this... this is different. It's not just feeling sad about a specific event. It's like the sadness has seeped into the concrete of my foundation, you know? 

I'm trying to think back... I mean, I've always been a pretty high-achieving person. In college, I was taking 18 credits a semester, working part-time, leading the engineering student council... I never stopped. And even early in my career, I was the one pulling all-nighters to get the project proposals done, just running on pure adrenaline and coffee. I felt unstoppable then. But this feeling right now, this absolute void... I don't know if I've ever felt it quite this deep or this intensely before. 

It's like... I remember a few years ago, maybe right before the promotion to senior project manager, I had a couple of weeks where I felt really sluggish and unmotivated, but I pushed through it. I always push through it. That's what you do in my field, you find a solution, you reinforce the structure. But this time, I can't find the structural flaw to fix. I don't know if I've ever felt this completely incapable of fixing it before. It's just... I don't know, it's hard to separate normal stress from whatever this is, but this feels so much worse than anything I can remember.
Can you recall if there have been other distinct periods in your life when you felt this same level of depression, or is this the first time you've experienced it?

Well, like I was saying, I've had times where I felt sluggish, but as for this exact level of... just total collapse? No, I don't think I've ever been this far down in the dark before. But as for this current feeling, this specific weight... it's been about a month now. 

I can actually trace it back pretty clearly, which is funny because usually everything feels so blurry lately. But it started right around the time the final financial settlement from the divorce came through. We had to divide up the assets, and he wanted half of the equity in the house—the house that I spent three years renovating, drawing up the plans for the extension, overseeing the contractors, literally pouring my own sweat into the foundation work. And suddenly I'm looking at these spreadsheets, these bank statements, trying to figure out how I'm going to buy him out without completely liquidating my retirement, and it just... hit me. 

It was a Tuesday, I think. I was sitting at my kitchen island with all these papers spread out, and I just couldn't look at the numbers anymore. It was like a physical switch flipped in my brain. Since then—so yeah, about four, maybe four and a half weeks now—it's just been this constant, suffocating fog. I wake up with it, I drag it to the office with me, I bring it home. It's been a solid month of just feeling like the ground under my feet is completely gone, all tied back to that financial mess with the divorce. It's just relentless. I keep waiting for it to lift, even just a little bit, but it hasn't budged an inch in four weeks.

Since this is the first time you've felt this level of depression, can you tell me if you've ever had any other periods in your life where you felt significantly depressed for a period of two weeks or more, and if so, how long ago those were?

I... well, I mean, I don't really think so? Not for two whole weeks, not like this. Like I mentioned before, maybe a few years ago I had a sluggish couple of weeks before that promotion, but even then, I wouldn't call it being significantly depressed. I was still functioning, you know? I was still getting up, going to the site, reviewing the CAD files, arguing with the city inspectors over zoning permits. I was tired, sure, and maybe a little unmotivated, but I wasn't... I wasn't drowning. 

I really try to keep things moving. In my job, if you stop, the whole project stops, and you lose thousands of dollars a day in delays. So I've never really allowed myself to just stop for two weeks. If I felt down, I'd throw myself into a new schematic or take on extra site visits. I'd distract myself with the math, with the concrete, with the steel. Steel is reliable, you know? It has a predictable tensile strength. Human emotions... not so much. 

So, no, I can't really point to a time in my past where I was just down in a hole for two solid weeks or more. Even when things were bad with my ex-husband before the divorce, when we were arguing all the time about my hours at work and how I was never home, I'd feel terrible for a day or two, maybe cry in my car on the way to the office, but by the time I put my hard hat on, I had boxed it up. I had compartmentalized it. I'm usually so good at compartmentalizing. That's why this current thing is so terrifying. The boxes are all broken. But yeah, to answer your question, no, I don't think there's ever been a two-week period of real depression before this last month. This is all new territory for me, and I don't have a map for it.
Have you ever had a period in your life before this last month where you felt persistently down, hopeless, or unable to function for at least two weeks at a time?

Well, like I was trying to explain, no, not before this past month. I mean, I've never been the type of person to just stop functioning. That's actually why I finally made the appointment to come in and see you, because this... this is entirely different. I came in because I just can't shake this incredibly heavy, completely hopeless feeling. It's like... it's like everything I built after the divorce, all the careful planning and the structural reinforcements I put into my own life, it's all just collapsed. 

And I'm just sitting under it. Like a building that's pancaked on itself, and I'm trapped under the concrete slabs, and there's no heavy machinery coming to dig me out. I just sit there under the weight of it all. I can't even describe how dense it feels. It's not just a passing sadness, it's a physical weight that makes it hard to breathe, hard to think, hard to even care about the projects I used to be so passionate about. I used to look at a set of blueprints and see possibilities, see a structure rising up from the dirt. Now I just look at them and see... nothing. Just lines on paper. 

So, no, before these last four weeks, I've never had a two-week stretch where I felt this utterly defeated and unable to function. I've always been the one holding it all together, making sure the load-bearing walls are secure. But right now, I feel like the foundation has completely given way, and I'm just buried under the rubble, completely hopeless.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down or hopeless nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?

I feel like I'm repeating myself, but... no. Not before this last month. I mean, I really just came in because I can't shake this heavy, hopeless feeling right now. It's like everything I built after the divorce, all the careful planning, the structural reinforcements I put into my own life... it's all just collapsed, and I'm just sitting under it. 

I've never felt anything like this before. Like I said, I've always been the one holding it all together, making sure the load-bearing walls are secure. If things got tough, I'd just work harder. I'd take on more projects, do more site visits, focus on the math and the materials. I've never had a time where I just... couldn't. Where I felt this down, this hopeless, every single day for weeks on end. It's just this last month. This one, horrible, relentless month where I feel like I'm buried under the rubble of my own life and I can't even find the energy to try and dig myself out.
